misconception: Without you watching, it all falls apart — nothing can run reliably on its own.

mentorLessons.line: A scheduled task fires on its own clock — hourly, daily, weekdays — and each firing starts a fresh session. Write the prompt as a complete standalone instruction, because the run remembers nothing.
Work scheduled to the cloud runs remotely — it keeps going while your laptop sleeps. Work bound to an open session stops the moment that session ends. Know which kind you built.
Wire Claude into GitHub Actions and a simple @claude mention in a PR or issue summons it — analyzing code, fixing bugs, opening pull requests, all following your project's CLAUDE.md standards.

A subagent works in its own context window and hands back only the summary. Delegate the noisy exploration; keep your main thread clean. Independent tasks can run as separate subagents simultaneously.
The Messages API is stateless: every request stands alone. If you want Claude to remember the conversation, your code sends the whole history back each time. That's not a flaw — it's your control.
Tool use is a contract: Claude never runs your function itself. It returns a structured request — this tool, these arguments — your code executes it and sends the result back. The loop is the power.

When every call carries the same heavy prefix — system prompt, big document, tool definitions — prompt caching lets Claude reread it from cache instead of reprocessing it. Stable content in front, changing content behind.

The Agent SDK is Claude Code's harness as a library — the tools, agent loop, and context management, programmable in Python and TypeScript. Raw API when you want a completion; Agent SDK when you want an agent that acts.

Match the automation to the trigger: a clock says scheduled task, a repository event says GitHub Actions, a big side-investigation says subagent, a custom product says the API or Agent SDK. The Spire has a floor for each.

questions.prompt: You want a briefing summarizing your connected tools' activity waiting for you every weekday at 9am — without ever opening Claude to ask. What do you set up?
choices: Nothing works — Claude only runs while you're actively watching it
A very long single chat you keep open forever
A scheduled task on a weekday recurrence — each run executes on its own and you review the result
A Project with the request in its instructions
questions.reteach: Scheduled tasks run recurring work on a set cadence — hourly, daily, weekly, or weekdays — with no manual restart.
hardChoices: A /loop in an open Claude Code session set to fire every weekday morning
A GitHub Actions workflow — CI is the standard way to run anything on a schedule
An Agent SDK script you run manually each morning to generate the briefing

questions.prompt: Your scheduled task's prompt says "continue what we discussed." Why will this fail?
choices: Each firing starts a fresh, independent session — the prompt must be a complete standalone instruction
Scheduled tasks can't accept prompts longer than one word
It won't fail — every run remembers the chat where you created it
Scheduled prompts must be written in cron syntax
questions.reteach: Every scheduled run is its own independent session with no memory of past conversations, so write the prompt to stand entirely alone.
hardChoices: The task binds to your chat but only keeps the last few messages of context
Scheduled runs share memory only with other runs of the same task, not your chat
It fails only if the task runs in the cloud; desktop tasks keep the chat context

questions.prompt: Your scheduled task fires at 6am while your laptop is closed and asleep. What happens with a cloud-scheduled task?
choices: It fails — Claude can't do anything while your machine is off
It runs anyway — cloud tasks execute remotely and don't need your machine on
It waits at the login screen until you wake the laptop
It runs at half speed using your laptop's reserve battery
questions.reteach: Cloud scheduled tasks execute remotely, so they keep running even when your computer sleeps or the app is closed.
hardChoices: It runs only if the Claude desktop app was left open in the background
It queues and fires immediately the next time your laptop wakes
It runs remotely but can't use connected tools until your machine is back online

questions.prompt: In Claude Code you set a /loop to re-check a deploy every 10 minutes, then close the terminal for the night. What actually happens?
choices: The loop keeps firing forever — /loop runs in the cloud
The loop transfers itself to GitHub automatically
Claude Code emails you the results instead
The loop stops firing — /loop is session-scoped; unattended work needs a cloud/desktop scheduled task or CI instead
questions.reteach: Session-scoped loops only fire while the session is running — durable unattended scheduling belongs in cloud tasks, desktop tasks, or CI.
hardChoices: The loop hands off to a cloud scheduled task automatically when the session ends
It keeps firing as long as your laptop stays awake, even with the terminal closed
The final loop iteration completes in the background, then it stops

questions.prompt: With Claude Code GitHub Actions installed on your repo, a teammate types "@claude fix the TypeError in the dashboard component" in an issue comment. What can happen next?
choices: Claude analyzes the code and can implement the fix and open a pull request — following the repo's CLAUDE.md standards
Nothing — Claude can't be triggered from inside GitHub
GitHub forwards the comment to your personal chat for you to handle live
Claude replies with advice but can never touch code from CI
questions.reteach: A simple @claude mention in a PR or issue can have Claude analyze code, implement fixes, and create pull requests, guided by your CLAUDE.md.
hardChoices: Claude analyzes and comments a suggested diff, but a human must open the PR
It works only on pull request comments, not issue comments
Claude opens a PR but ignores CLAUDE.md — CI runs don't read repo config files

questions.prompt: You're adding the Claude API key to your GitHub Actions workflow. What's the correct handling?
choices: Paste it directly into the workflow YAML so it's easy to find
Post it in the repo README with a warning not to copy it
Store it as a GitHub repository secret and reference the secret in the workflow
Commit it in a file named do-not-read.txt
questions.reteach: Never commit API keys — store them as GitHub Secrets and reference the secret name in the workflow.
hardChoices: Store it in CLAUDE.md so Claude reads it automatically on each run
Put it in an untracked .env file in the repo — Actions loads it automatically
Base64-encode it in the workflow YAML so it isn't stored in plain text

questions.prompt: A research side-task would flood your main Claude Code conversation with search results and file dumps you'll never reference again. Best move?
choices: Do it in the main thread and scroll past the noise later
Delegate it to a subagent — it works in its own context window and returns only the summary
Restart the whole session after every search
Paste the results into a second monitor
questions.reteach: A subagent does noisy exploration in its own context window and hands back only the conclusion, keeping your main conversation clean.
hardChoices: Use prompt caching so the search results are cached instead of filling context
Run it in the main thread but ask Claude to compact the context afterward
Spawn a scheduled task to do the research on its own recurring cadence

questions.prompt: You need the authentication, database, and API modules each investigated independently. What does Claude Code let you do?
choices: Only one investigation per day is allowed
Nothing — you must personally supervise each investigation in sequence or the results can't be trusted
Merge all three into one giant prompt so nothing is missed
Spawn a separate subagent for each module and run them in parallel
questions.reteach: Independent investigations can run as multiple subagents simultaneously, each in its own context, reporting findings back.
hardChoices: Run one subagent three times in sequence — subagents can't run concurrently
Open three scheduled tasks so each module is investigated on its own clock
Ask the Messages API directly — parallel work needs stateless API calls

questions.prompt: A developer asks what the Messages API fundamentally is. Best answer?
choices: A stateless request/response endpoint: you send a model choice, messages, and parameters; Claude returns a response — no server-side conversation memory
A live socket where Claude remembers every user forever
A file-sync service for uploading documents
A dashboard for monitoring Claude's mood
questions.reteach: The Messages API is stateless request/response — each call is independent, and any conversation memory is content you send.
hardChoices: A stateful endpoint that stores each conversation server-side under a thread ID
Claude Code's agent loop exposed over HTTP with built-in tool execution
A managed hosting service that runs your agent and its tools in Anthropic's cloud

questions.prompt: Your app's users complain Claude "forgets" everything they said one message ago. As the developer, what's the actual bug?
choices: The model is broken and needs a restart
You need to shout the context in capital letters
Your code isn't including the prior messages in each request — the stateless API only knows what you send it
Claude only remembers paying users
questions.reteach: Because the API is stateless, your application must send the conversation history with every request — omit it and Claude genuinely has never seen it.
hardChoices: You forgot to enable the API's session mode, which persists chats server-side
Prompt caching is off — the cache is what carries memory between calls
You should switch to the Agent SDK — only agents can remember prior turns

questions.prompt: You define a lookup_order tool for your support bot. When Claude decides to use it, what actually happens?
choices: Claude reaches into your database directly and runs the query itself
Claude returns a structured request naming the tool and arguments — your code executes it and sends the result back for Claude to use
The tool definition alone teaches Claude every order in the database
Claude emails your DBA to run it manually
questions.reteach: For your own tools, Claude requests the call; your application executes it and returns the result — Claude never runs your code itself.
hardChoices: Claude executes the tool in a managed sandbox and returns the query results
The API server runs your function and injects the output into Claude's reply
Claude calls your database only after you approve each request in the console

questions.prompt: Which job is the reason you'd reach for tool use in the first place?
choices: Letting Claude fetch live data or act on external systems it couldn't otherwise touch — like querying today's inventory
Making Claude's prose more poetic
Reducing the length of Claude's answers
Encrypting the conversation
questions.reteach: Tool use exists to connect Claude to live data and external actions — things outside what any prompt alone could contain.
hardChoices: Guaranteeing structured JSON output — tool use is mainly a formatting feature
Caching heavy tool definitions so repeated calls get cheaper and faster
Letting Claude run its own code server-side without your app in the loop

questions.prompt: Your product sends the same 80-page policy manual plus system prompt on every one of thousands of daily API calls; only the user's question changes. What concept directly targets this waste?
choices: Asking users to read the manual themselves
Deleting the manual — rules are a vibe
Prompt caching — the stable prefix is cached and reused across calls, cutting cost and latency instead of reprocessing it every time
Sending the manual only on odd-numbered requests
questions.reteach: Prompt caching reuses a stable prompt prefix across many calls, so repeated heavy content is read from cache instead of reprocessed.
hardChoices: Tool use — register the manual as a tool so Claude fetches it only when needed
The Agent SDK's context management, which compacts the manual automatically
A scheduled task that pre-loads the manual into every future session

questions.prompt: Which content is the RIGHT candidate for prompt caching?
choices: The part that changes on every single request
Stable, repeated content — system prompts, large reference documents, tool definitions
Random numbers you generate per call
Nothing — caching applies to model weights, not prompts
questions.reteach: Caching pays off on stable reused content like system prompts, big documents, and tool definitions — not on parts that vary per request.
hardChoices: The user's newest question, since it's the part Claude reads most carefully
Tool results returned mid-conversation — caching targets outputs, not inputs
Whole conversations, so the API can restore them server-side between sessions

questions.prompt: What does the Claude Agent SDK actually give a developer?
choices: A no-code website builder
A faster internet connection to the API
A GUI theme for the terminal
Claude Code's harness as a library — built-in tools, the agent loop, and context management, programmable in Python and TypeScript
questions.reteach: The Agent SDK packages the tools, agent loop, and context management that power Claude Code into a library you drive from Python or TypeScript.
hardChoices: A hosted service where Anthropic runs your agent's tools on their servers
A thin HTTP wrapper over the Messages API with no tools or loop included
Claude Code's terminal UI repackaged — scripting it still requires the CLI open

questions.prompt: You're building an agent that must autonomously read files, run commands, and edit code inside a pipeline. Raw Messages API or Agent SDK — and why?
choices: Agent SDK — with the raw API you'd implement the whole tool-execution loop yourself; the SDK ships it built in
Raw API — SDKs are only for beginners
Neither — autonomous file editing is impossible from any program
Raw API — it includes a built-in file editor already
questions.reteach: With direct API access you implement tool execution yourself; the Agent SDK ships built-in tools and the agent loop, which is exactly what an autonomous agent needs.
hardChoices: Raw API — tool use means Claude already executes files and commands itself
Agent SDK — the raw Messages API doesn't support tool use at all
Either works the same — the SDK is just the API client with retries added

questions.prompt: SYNTHESIS: You want a weekly report compiled from your connected tools' data, delivered every Monday without anyone asking. What do you combine?
choices: A really detailed one-time prompt you re-paste each Monday
A scheduled task on a weekly cadence whose standalone prompt uses your connected tools
It can't be trusted — automation falls apart the moment no one is watching
A subagent inside a chat you promise not to close
questions.reteach: Recurring unattended deliverables are a scheduled task: a weekly recurrence plus a standalone prompt that draws on your connected tools.
hardChoices: A subagent spawned each Monday — subagents fire on their own recurring clock
A GitHub Actions cron workflow — connected-tool reports are a CI job
A cloud session left open with a /loop set to a seven-day interval

questions.prompt: SYNTHESIS: Match the trigger to the tool — work that must run on every pull request in your repository belongs in…
choices: A daily scheduled task that hopefully coincides with PRs
A /loop you keep alive in a terminal forever
GitHub Actions — CI reacts to repository events like a PR opening, which no clock-based schedule can do
A Project instruction saying "watch the repo"
questions.reteach: Clock-driven work is a scheduled task; event-driven repository work — like reacting to every PR — is CI via GitHub Actions.
hardChoices: An hourly scheduled task that polls the repo for new pull requests
An Agent SDK script on your laptop subscribed to live PR events
A cloud scheduled task — cloud runs can react to repository events
